findings.detail: Graph construction does not recover each training sequence. It concatenates every row's history and target independently, then counts all adjacent pairs. In the common prefix/target training format, the same user sequence is represented by multiple overlapping prefixes; this repeatedly weights earlier edges, while the requested C counts adjacent pairs once per training sequence. The degree is correspondingly not the specified out-degree. This changes the weighting/consensus mechanism, not merely its implementation.
findings.reproduction: One true sequence [a,b,c] represented as prefix rows ([a],b) and ([a,b],c) produces counts a→b=2 and b→c=1; the specified one-pass sequence count gives 1 for both. With further overlapping prefixes, early edges are increasingly overcounted.
findings.correction: Construct the graph from the frozen training sequence source with one ordered sequence per user (or deduplicate/reconstruct sequences according to the frozen schema), and count each adjacent pair once. Do not join independent rows as if each row were a separate observed sequence.

findings.detail: Only GRAPH_LAMBDA=0.1 is actually trained. There is no run over {0.1,0.3,0.5} and no validation-based selection protocol in this entry point; the comment delegates selection downstream, but no parameterized lambda/run manifest or validation integration is implemented. Thus the specified candidate comparison is not integrated.
findings.reproduction: Inspect main(): denoise_with_train_transitions is called once without strength at line 296, so every invocation uses 0.1 and exports only that candidate.
findings.correction: Make lambda an explicit candidate configuration and run the three candidates with identical tokenizer settings; select only using the predeclared validation protocol, recording the selected value and candidate outputs.
